notes: Renders a NATIVE `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`. The previous note here claimed the native element was rejected because it cannot be portalled and brings a stacking model this approach cannot reason about. BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG: a modal `<dialog>` can be portalled anywhere in the DOM, is never clipped by an ancestor's `overflow: hidden`, and cannot be trapped by an ancestor `transform` — none of which is true of the hand-rolled fixed div it replaced.

Focus containment, background inertness, focus restoration and Escape are all supplied by the platform. Measured, not assumed: a programmatic `.focus()` on a button behind the open dialog is REFUSED, and `elementFromPoint` over that button returns the dialog. The contract states all four in prose and can declare none of them; they follow from an element name.

It is opened by CALLING `showModal()` from an effect, never by rendering the `open` attribute — React sets the attribute on the first render and `showModal()` then throws `InvalidStateError`. This is the FIRST `useEffect` in generated code, and the first time a generated component has held a ref to its own root.

The open state is synced back from the element's own `open` attribute through a `MutationObserver`, NOT from the `close` event. Measured: `close` did not fire in Chrome 153 — not through React's `onClose` prop, not through `addEventListener`, and not through the `onclose` property, on this element or on a bare probe dialog. a11y-dialog documents the same unreliability. The observer also catches every other way the platform can close the element behind the component's back.

Getting that sync wrong is not cosmetic. Once the state says open and the element says closed, the effect sees no change, `showModal()` is never called again, and the dialog can never be shown for the rest of the session. That failure was reached during the spike.

The scrim is `::backdrop` and is declared by the root's `backdrop` block rather than as a part, because on this platform IT IS NOT ONE: it cannot hold a child, carry an attribute, or be an event target. That last point is why backdrop-press dismissal is NOT supplied — a press on the backdrop reports the dialog itself as the target.

The theme file now opens with a reset that cancels the UA stylesheet's border, padding, background, colour and max-inline-size. That reset is a real cost and was accepted deliberately: consumers of this library bring their own token system, so cancelling browser defaults is work they were always going to do.

`Dialog.structure.css` carries `:not([open]) { display: none !important }` alongside the `[hidden]` rule. `dialog:not([open]) { display: none }` is a browser-stylesheet rule and any `display` a theme puts on the element outranks it — the same cascade trap that previously left this component permanently on screen, under a different selector.
